texts: good. "Cauldron Hall" stays one name symbol with its separate hall type atom, and the keeping event carries agent and object with no tense atom, which is the right habitual reading.

bad: the four tracked fields are stacked as four objects on a single tracking event, a shape reserved for joint or reciprocal actions; a coordinated object list should become one predication per item, so as parsed the four fields are welded into one act and no per-record tracking is derivable. Split the list into one clause per field: "The records track thread weight. The records track sea-water source. The records track boil time. The records track vessel yield."
good. the definite plural "the records" becomes a group, and the non-benefit "for seasonal planning" goes to the preposition-named oblique with the compound decomposed.

mixed: every atom is well-formed, but the parse reads as one fixed apprentice serving every season — the numeral "one" has no carrier on a singular noun, and nothing marks that the apprentice varies from season to season. State the two facts in separate clauses: "A single apprentice serves at Cauldron Hall each season. A new apprentice takes the post each season."

good. the name, the location on the serving event, past tense and the (Year 1) term are all carried; the bare season symbol is an unguided extension of the time vocabulary, but that is an instruction-set gap rather than a problem with your wording.
good. "briefly" correctly becomes a duration rather than a manner, and the name, location, season, year and past tense are all present.
